metadata.title: Coherent Torsion Electromagnetic Catapult for Lunar Surface-to-Orbit Mass Transport
metadata.description:
We present the ARKHE OS Lunar Mass Driver (LMD-127), a conceptual
engineering design specication for a coherent torsion electromagnetic catapult
system intended to operate on the lunar south pole, within the ARKHE OS
v127 ecosystem. The system is designed to launch payloads of 50500 kg from
the lunar surface to transfer orbits (LEO, GEO, or Lagrange points) at an exit
velocity of 2,400 m/s, without conventional chemical propellant.
The LMD-127 introduces ve primary innovations: (i) Active Torsion Metamaterial Rails employing CVD diamond with nitrogen-vacancy (nv) centres excited at 532 nm for coherent electromagnetic torsion eld generation; (ii) the
PLANK Launch Ceremony, a quantum-nonce cryptographic authorisation protocol based on photon polarisation measurement; (iii) an LLM-FPGA compiler
(Substrate 123) for real-time translation of launch specications into partial
FPGA bitstreams with formal verication; (iv) a Multi-Armed Bandit UCB1
optimisation engine for continuous parameter tuning; and (v) a 7-Dimensional
Coherence Monitor (Temporal, Spatial, Energetic, Cryptographic, Torsion, Integrity, and Sovereignty) for holistic launch integrity assurance.
ARKHE LMD-127: Coherent Torsion Electromagnetic Launch System Oliveira, 2026
The system architecture integrates 24 rail modules of 50 m each (total 1,200 m),
a hybrid power subsystem (15 MW solar, 50 MW/30 s smes, 120 MWh Li-ion,
800 MJ pulse capacitors), and a three-level hierarchical control architecture with
deterministic latency below 100 µs. Operational throughput is specied at up to
6 launches per hour (3 t/h), with a target system availability of 99.7%. Total
project cost is estimated at US$5.95 billion over a 39-month deployment timeline.
Security architecture follows a hardware-rst, zero-trust paradigm: a hardware Safety Enclave with deterministic veto latency below 10 µs, a Zero-Knowledge
Assurance Lattice for external auditability, and full integration with the ARKHE
decentralised identity and distributed ledger infrastructure. This document constitutes a conceptual engineering design specification in the Design Fiction as
Epistemic Practice (dfep) methodology framework [1].
